mainTopic: How the prohibition of בל תאחר (do not delay a vow) can apply to a נזיר
overview: The גמרא is looking for a way a person who vowed נזירות could break בל תאחר, the rule against delaying a vow. רב אחא בר יעקב suggests someone who vowed while in a cemetery. The answer holds even if the נזירות starts right away, because he is still putting off a pure נזירות. From this, רב אשי rules that a נזיר who makes himself טמא on purpose also breaks בל תאחר. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says the delay can be in the final shaving, and מר זוטרא says it can be in the קרבנות. The גמרא then asks why we need the נזיר source for the קרבנות, since the פסוק 'כי דרש ידרשנו' already covers חטאות and אשמות. It answers that נזיר is a חידוש, and then tries to pin down what that חידוש is. Two suggestions are rejected, and a third begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: A vow made in a cemetery
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the earlier question: בל תאחר applies to a נזיר who vowed while in a cemetery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: This happens, for example, when he made the vow while he was in a cemetery.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the question from just before this: how can a נזיר ever break בל תאחר? His case is someone who vowed נזירות while standing in a cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר may not be in a place of טומאת מת like a cemetery. So the idea is that his נזירות cannot properly begin until he leaves and becomes pure. If he stays there, he is holding back his own vow, and that counts as delaying it.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not delay: the prohibition against putting off the fulfillment of a vow
The status of being a נזיר (no wine, no haircut, no contact with the dead)
Cemetery
For example, such as

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
For example, where he vowed while he was in a cemetery.
phrases.notes: He is answering the question just before this: how can a נזיר ever break בל תאחר?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דִּנְדַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from earlier in the daf about how בל תאחר can apply to נזירות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person who vowed נזירות while inside a cemetery delays his vow by staying there.

steps.title: This only works if the vow does not start right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the answer only works for the view that נזירות does not start in the cemetery. If it starts immediately, nothing is delayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says the naziriteship does not take effect on him immediately. But according to the one who says it takes effect on him immediately, is there any 'do not delay' here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אחא בר יעקב. His case only makes sense for one opinion about when נזירות begins for someone in a cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת about whether נזירות begins for someone who vowed in a cemetery. If it does not begin until he leaves, staying there delays it. But if it begins at once, then his vow is already in force, so what is he delaying?

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one view, but not for another)
According to the one who says
Takes effect, starts to apply
Immediately, right away

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
the naziriteship does not take effect on him immediately.
But according to the one who says
it takes effect on him immediately,
is there any 'do not delay'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's cemetery case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the נזירות takes effect right away, his vow is already being kept, so there is no delay.

steps.title: Everyone agrees it starts right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes the challenge stronger: מר בר רב אשי said everyone agrees נזירות starts at once, and the argument is only about lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, didn't מר בר רב אשי say: the naziriteship takes effect on him immediately, and when they argue, it is only about lashes that they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger point. According to מר בר רב אשי, nobody says the נזירות waits, so רב אחא בר יעקב's case seems not to work for anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 2 the problem was only with one opinion. Now מר בר רב אשי says all opinions agree the נזירות starts right away. The only argument is whether he gets מלקות for breaking נזיר rules while still in the cemetery. So the delay idea looks weaker than before.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: introduces an extra point
They argue, disagree
Regarding, with respect to
Lashes, the punishment of flogging

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד: הָאָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't Mar bar Rav Ashi say:
the naziriteship takes effect on him immediately,
and when they argue, it is regarding lashes that they argue!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: הָאָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 2 by showing that all opinions hold the נזירות starts right away.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's cemetery case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everyone agrees the נזירות starts immediately, no opinion is left for which staying in the cemetery delays the vow.

steps.title: He is delaying a pure נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: even though the נזירות started, he is delaying the pure נזירות he is supposed to keep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, he is in violation of 'do not delay,' because he is delaying a naziriteship of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אחא בר יעקב. Yes, the נזירות already applies, but he still breaks בל תאחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is meant to keep his days of נזירות in a state of טהרה. Days spent impure in a cemetery do not count toward that pure period. By staying there, he pushes off the pure נזירות he promised, so he is delaying his vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
A naziriteship kept in a state of ritual purity
Delays, puts off

steps.whatToRemember: Even if נזירות starts right away, the נזיר still owes a pure נזירות. Holding that back counts as בל תאחר.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי קָם לֵיהּ בְּ״בַל תְּאַחֵר״,
phrases.english: Even so, he is in violation of 'do not delay,'
because he is delaying a naziriteship of purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenge assumed that once נזירות applies, nothing is being delayed.
steps.terutzMaskana: What is delayed is the pure נזירות, which cannot be kept while he stays impure in the cemetery.

steps.title: A נזיר who makes himself impure on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי builds on this: a נזיר who makes himself impure on purpose breaks בל תאחר, because he delays his pure נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Since this is so, a נזיר who made himself impure on purpose transgresses 'do not delay' of a naziriteship of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the idea from step 4 and applies it to a new case. If delaying pure נזירות is בל תאחר, then a נזיר who makes himself טמא on purpose also breaks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a נזיר becomes טמא, his pure days are lost and he must start again. If he does this deliberately, he is pushing off the end of his pure נזירות. So he breaks בל תאחר too, on top of the ban on becoming impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Since this is so
Made himself ritually impure
On purpose, deliberately
Transgresses

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the new idea of a 'pure נזירות' brings a new חיוב: a deliberate טומאה is also a delay of the vow.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Since this is so,
a nazir who made himself impure on purpose
transgresses 'do not delay' of a naziriteship of purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the answer of step 4 to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר who deliberately makes himself impure breaks בל תאחר, because he delays his pure נזירות.

steps.title: Delaying the final shaving
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא gives a different case: a נזיר breaks בל תאחר by delaying his shaving at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא said: He transgresses 'do not delay' regarding his shaving.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives another answer to the original question. For him, בל תאחר comes up when the נזיר delays his shaving at the end of his נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the end of his term, a נזיר must shave his hair and bring קרבנות. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says the delay is in putting off this shaving. This is a separate approach from the cemetery case.

keyTerms.meaning: His shaving: the haircut a נזיר does at the end of his term
Son of

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to find בל תאחר for a נזיר: staying impure in a cemetery, which delays a pure נזירות, or delaying the shaving at the end.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika said:
he transgresses 'do not delay' regarding his shaving.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the original question that step 1 answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נזיר breaks בל תאחר by delaying his end-of-term shaving.

steps.title: Delaying the shaving works for both opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא's answer works even for the view that shaving is not required, because he still has not done the מצוה of shaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious for the view that shaving holds him back. Even for the view that shaving does not hold him back, at least he has not done the מצוה of shaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is widening רב אחא's answer from step 6. It shows that delaying the shaving breaks בל תאחר according to both opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that a נזיר stays a נזיר until he shaves, so delaying the shaving clearly delays his vow. Others hold that his נזירות ends once he brings his קרבנות, even without shaving. The גמרא says that even by that view, he still has a מצוה of shaving left undone, so delaying it is still a delay.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say (this case is obvious; the next case is the real point)
The shaving a נזיר does at the end of his נזירות
Holds back / is required (without it, the process is not complete)
At least / in any case

phrases.english: And it is not necessary to say
according to the one who says shaving is required,
but even according to the one who says
shaving is not required,
at least he has not fulfilled the מצוה of shaving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב אחא's answer so it fits both opinions about shaving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delaying the shaving breaks בל תאחר by both opinions, because at the very least the מצוה of shaving is still undone.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: delaying the offerings
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי gives another case: a נזיר breaks בל תאחר by delaying his קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, son of רב מרי, said: he breaks בל תאחר with his קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא offers another answer to the question of how a נזיר breaks בל תאחר. His answer: by delaying the קרבנות he must bring at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a נזיר finishes, he must bring קרבנות. If he puts them off, he is delaying something he owes, just like delaying a vowed קרבן. This answer is about the offerings, not the shaving or keeping pure נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: His offerings (the קרבנות a נזיר brings when his term ends)
The prohibition 'do not delay' fulfilling a vow

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari said:
He transgresses 'You shall not delay' with his offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the original question, alongside רב אחא בר יעקב (step 1, cemetery) and רב אחא בריה דרב איקא (step 6, shaving), this time about the offerings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נזיר breaks בל תאחר by delaying his קרבנות.

steps.title: Offerings already have their own source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why learn this from the נזיר case, when the פסוק 'כי דרש ידרשנו' already covers all חטאות and אשמות?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we learn this from here? We already learn it from there: 'for He will surely require it.' These are חטאות and אשמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר זוטרא's answer. Delaying any חטאת or אשם is already forbidden by a different פסוק, so why do we need the נזיר source for it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא learned that a נזיר is included in בל תאחר from the link between vows and נזירות. But if that link only teaches 'do not delay his קרבנות', it seems useless, because the פסוק 'כי דרש ידרשנו' already teaches that חטאות and אשמות fall under בל תאחר. The נזיר's offerings include a חטאת and an אשם, so they should already be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it out / it is derived
'He will surely require it,' a phrase in the פסוק about בל תאחר
Sin-offerings
Guilt-offerings

phrases.english: And is it derived from here?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the link between vows and נזירות that taught us a נזיר is included in בל תאחר.

phrases.english: It is derived from there:
'For He will surely require it'
these are sin-offerings and guilt-offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִן הָכָא נָפְקָא לֵיהּ? מֵהָתָם נָפְקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks מר זוטרא's answer by showing that a separate source already covers it.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that the נזיר source teaches 'do not delay his קרבנות'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'כי דרש ידרשנו' already puts חטאות and אשמות under בל תאחר, the נזיר source would teach nothing new.

steps.title: A נזיר's offerings might have been unique
steps.stepSummary: The special source is needed, because otherwise we might think the נזיר's קרבנות are a unique חידוש of the Torah and do not follow the normal rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: it is a new rule the Torah made just for a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Without the special source, we could have thought the נזיר's offerings are a one-of-a-kind rule, so the general פסוק would not apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the נזיר's case is a חידוש, a one-of-a-kind Torah rule, and normal rules are not automatically applied to a חידוש. So the general rule for חטאות and אשמות might not have covered it, and the נזיר source is still needed. The גמרא does not yet say what the חידוש is; steps 11-16 try to define it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken thought the source prevents)
A new, unusual rule that cannot be compared to other cases

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר can break בל תאחר by delaying his pure נזירות, his shaving, or his קרבנות. The נזיר source is still needed for the קרבנות because נזיר is a חידוש. The next steps work out what that חידוש is.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is a novelty that the Torah made new for a nazir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 and defends מר זוטרא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the extra source is needed to block a mistaken conclusion (מהו דתימא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נזיר's קרבנות are a unique חידוש, so the general rule for חטאות and אשמות would not apply to them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נזיר source teaches that even these unique קרבנות fall under בל תאחר.

steps.title: What exactly is the חידוש of a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unique חידוש of נזיר is, and suggests it might be that a נזיר's חטאת cannot be taken on through a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the חידוש? If you say it is that a person cannot take on a נזיר's חטאת through a vow...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the 'חידוש' from step 10 actually is. It also suggests a first possible answer, which it will test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 claimed the נזיר's offerings are a חידוש, so the גמרא wants to know exactly what is new about them. The first proposal: a person who is not a נזיר cannot say 'I will bring a נזיר's חטאת.' That offering cannot be taken on through a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Something new or unusual in the Torah that does not follow the normal rules
If you say (it introduces a suggestion that will probably be rejected)
Takes upon himself or obligates himself (here, through a vow)
The sin-offering a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות

phrases.english: What is the novelty?
If you say that one cannot take upon himself
the sin-offering of a נזיר through a vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the חידוש mentioned in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is unique about a נזיר's offerings, such that we might think בל תאחר does not apply to them?

steps.title: A regular חטאת חלב is the same, so that is not a חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: a חטאת חלב also cannot be taken on through a vow, yet בל תאחר applies to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a חטאת for eating חלב also cannot be taken on through a vow, and still one transgresses בל תאחר by delaying it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first suggestion. Many normal offerings also cannot be taken on through a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת חלב comes only when someone sinned. Nobody can volunteer to bring one, yet בל תאחר still applies to it. So 'cannot be vowed' is not special to a נזיר, and it would not make us think בל תאחר does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering brought for eating forbidden fat by accident
The prohibition against delaying the fulfillment of a vow or offering
But look at (it points out a counter-example)

phrases.english: But there is the sin-offering for forbidden fat,
which one cannot take on through a vow,
and yet one transgresses 'Do not delay'!
phrases.notes: In other words, the חטאת חלב is already covered by the general פסוק 'כי דרש ידרשנו' from step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the חידוש is the inability to take on a נזיר's חטאת through a vow.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same is true of a regular חטאת חלב, and בל תאחר still applies, so this is not unusual at all.

steps.title: Second answer: a vow from grape seeds makes a full נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The חידוש is that someone who vows to be a נזיר even only from grape seeds becomes a נזיר in every way. So we might have thought בל תאחר does not apply, and the source teaches that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is its חידוש? You might have thought that because someone who says 'I am a נזיר even from grape seeds' becomes a נזיר for everything, he does not transgress בל תאחר. The Torah teaches us that he does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for what the נזיר's חידוש is. It explains why we needed the special source in the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a vow only covers what you said. Here, saying 'נזיר from grape seeds' makes you a נזיר in every way. Since נזירות works so differently from normal vows, we might think the vow rule of בל תאחר does not apply either, so the Torah has to teach that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces a mistaken first impression)
Grape seeds, one of the things a נזיר may not eat
A נזיר in every way, with all the restrictions
It teaches us (the source comes to rule out the mistaken idea)

phrases.english: Rather, what is its novelty?
It would enter your mind to say:
since if he said 'I am hereby a נזיר'

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ מִן חַרְצָן — הָוֵי נָזִיר לַכֹּל,
phrases.english: even only from grape seeds, he is a נזיר for everything,
I would say he does not transgress on it
because of 'Do not delay.'
So it teaches us that he does.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מַאי חִידּוּשֵׁיהּ — סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion from steps 11-12 with a new explanation of the חידוש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a partial נזיר vow makes one a full נזיר, unlike normal vows, maybe the normal vow rule of בל תאחר does not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The special source teaches that בל תאחר still applies to the נזיר.

steps.title: This does not work for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The answer works only for the view that a grape-seed vow makes a full נזיר. רבי שמעון holds one is not a נזיר unless he vows from everything, so for him there is no חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says a נזיר from grape seeds is a נזיר for everything. But according to רבי שמעון, who says he is not a נזיר until he vows from all of them, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 13. It shows that the answer does not fit everyone's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, a vow to be a נזיר only from grape seeds does not make him a נזיר at all. He must vow to keep all the נזיר restrictions. So for him this חידוש does not exist, and the explanation of why the special source is needed falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says (it introduces a challenge from another opinion)
A תנא who holds one is a נזיר only if he vows from everything
What can be said? (there seems to be no answer)

phrases.english: This works out for the one who said

phrases.aramaic: כִּי נָזִיר מִן חַרְצָן הָוֵי נָזִיר לַכֹּל,
phrases.english: that when one is a נזיר from grape seeds, he is a נזיר for everything,
but according to רבי שמעון, who said
one is not a נזיר until he vows to abstain from all of them,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the חידוש is 'a נזיר from grape seeds is a נזיר for everything.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון does not accept that rule, so according to him there is no חידוש, and the special source would have no purpose.

steps.title: A strict חידוש should not lead to a leniency
steps.stepSummary: Another challenge: the grape-seed rule is a stringency, so it should not make us think the נזיר is let off from בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: this חידוש is a stringency!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge to the answer in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Becoming a full נזיר from a small vow makes things stricter. It makes no sense that a strict חידוש would lead us to a leniency like not breaking בל תאחר. So it cannot be what would make us think בל תאחר does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introduces an additional challenge)
For stringency, making the law stricter

phrases.english: And furthermore: this novelty is a stringency!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge against step 13, on top of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of the חידוש in step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A strict חידוש cannot be the reason to think the law is lenient (no בל תאחר).

steps.title: Starting a third explanation of the חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new answer about what the נזיר's חידוש is. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is its חידוש? That you might have thought: since...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא drops the second answer and starts a third one, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier proposals failed, so the גמרא tries again with the same pattern: 'you might have thought, since...' The actual content of the new חידוש comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (it introduces the reason for the mistaken thought)

phrases.english: Rather, what is its novelty?
That it would enter your mind to say: since...
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מַאי חִידּוּשֵׁיהּ? דְּסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Abandons the answer of step 13 after the challenges in steps 14-15 and begins a new one.
